judgements.reason: Passage never mentions slavery, servitude or the slave trade, nor any 'in all their forms' phrasing.
No tribunals, remedy or enforcement actor named; but 'the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks' is adjacent and could be read as naming 'the law' as the protector.
Passage says nothing about penal charges, presumption of innocence, guilt or trials.
No mention of movement, residence, borders or States anywhere in the passage.
Passage mentions 'family' only as an object of interference; no marriage, spouses or consent condition.
No mention of property or of owning something alone/in association with others.
No mention of social security or of any capacity such as 'member of society'.
No mention of work, remuneration, pay or an existence worthy of human dignity.
No mention of rest, leisure, working hours or holidays.
No mention of any social or international order, nor of realizing the Declaration's rights.
No mention of States, groups or persons claiming a right to destroy the Declaration's rights.
No mention of freedom of movement, residence or State borders.
No mention of marriage, of men and women of full age, or of race/nationality/religion limitations.
No mention of government, authority or the will of the people.
No mention of remuneration, workers or human dignity in the passage.
'family' appears only as something protected from interference; no motherhood, childhood, care or assistance.
No mention of duties, community, or development of personality.

Torture and cruel/inhuman/degrading treatment are absent, but the passage shares the frame 'No one shall be subjected to ... nor to attacks upon his honour and reputation', which a reader could mistakenly offer as the answer.
No mention of a hearing, tribunal, equality or fairness/publicity of proceedings.
'law' occurs only as 'protection of the law'; no penal offence, act or omission, and no national/international law distinction.
No mention of asylum, prosecutions, crimes or the United Nations.
No mention of nationality or of any right to change something.
No mention of associations or of being compelled to belong to anything.
No mention of national effort, international co-operation or the realization of rights.
No mention of pay, work or discrimination.

The passage contains no 'right to security' and lists no situations of unemployment/sickness; its only list ('privacy, family, home or correspondence') concerns objects of interference, not security situations.
No mention of limitations on rights, morality, public order, general welfare or a democratic society.
The passage does not refer to the Declaration itself or to interpreting it as implying a right to destroy rights.
No mention of asylum, other countries or persecution.
No mention of marriage or of the consent of intending spouses.
No mention of taking part in government, directly or through representatives.
No mention of rest, leisure, working hours or paid holidays.
No mention of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood, old age or livelihood.
The passage never discusses limitations on the exercise of rights, but it does invoke 'the protection of the law', so 'by law' could be wrongly extracted.
No mention of recognition as a person before the law and no locative answer such as 'everywhere'; 'law' appears only as protection against interference.
No mention of a hearing, of rights and obligations being determined, or of criminal charges.
No mention of penalties, penal offences or the time an offence was committed.
No mention of marriage, founding a family, or any grounds that may not limit such a right; the only list concerns privacy, family, home and correspondence.

Partly answered by 'No one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence' -- 'home' reads as property and the condition 'arbitrary' is stated, so a careful reader can answer 'when it is arbitrary'.
No mention of economic, social and cultural rights or of anything indispensable for dignity; no countable set of rights is given.
